content.overview: Section 166 codifies duties of good faith, care, conflict avoidance, undue-gain prohibition, and a bar on assigning office.
content.glance: Section 166 codifies duties of good faith, care, conflict avoidance, undue-gain prohibition, and a bar on assigning office.
content.study: A director must act in accordance with the articles, in good faith to promote the objects of the company for the benefit of members as a whole and in the best interests of the company, employees, shareholders, community and environment. Due and reasonable care, skill and diligence, and independent judgment, are required. Conflicted situations require disclosure. A director shall not achieve or attempt an undue gain or advantage for self or relatives, partners or associates; such gain is held in trust for the company and is liable to be repaid. Office cannot be assigned. Contravention attracts a fine. The section sits alongside common-law fiduciary duties and specific conflict provisions such as s. 184 and s. 188; it does not replace them.

examples.title: Corporate opportunity
examples.body: Diverting a company opportunity to a relative can be undue gain held in trust.

examples.title: Assignment
examples.body: A director cannot assign the office to another person.

distinctions: Section 166 is the general duty code. Section 184 is disclosure of interest. Section 188 is related-party transactions. Section 447 is fraud, which needs the dishonest intent element.

misconceptions.correction: Section 166 codifies duties of good faith, care, conflict avoidance, undue-gain prohibition, and a bar on assigning office.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Are statutory duties confined to shareholders?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. Section 166 expressly includes employees, the community and the environment alongside members and the company.
